record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given an n-bit prime p, a generator g of the multiplicative group F*_p, an element a in F*_p, and a positive integer k, is there a positive integer x whose binary representation contains at most k ones such that a = g^x?

evidence.quote: Question: Is there a positive integer x whose binary representation has at most k 1's (that is, x has a Hamming weight of k) such that a = gx?
Bounded Hamming Weight Discrete Logarithm Open

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let p be an n-bit prime, let g be a generator of the multiplicative group F_p^* of the finite field with p elements, let a ∈ F_p^*, and let k be a positive integer (the parameter). The Hamming weight of a positive integer x is the number of 1's in its binary representation. Determine the parameterized complexity, with parameter k, of the following decision problem: does there exist a positive integer x with Hamming weight at most k such that g^x ≡ a (mod p)? In particular, is this problem fixed-parameter tractable in k (i.e., solvable in time f(k) · poly(n) for some computable function f), or is it hard for some level of the W-hierarchy?
artifact.status_search_result: The parameterized complexity of the Bounded Hamming Weight Discrete Logarithm problem (with the Hamming weight bound k as parameter) is widely cited as an open problem of Downey and Fellows; it is known to lie in XP. While there are cryptographic algorithms improving the brute-force/meet-in-the-middle complexity (e.g., works by Coppersmith, Stinson, and recent low-weight DL algorithms), and an FPT result is known for the bounded sum-of-digits variant in certain finite field settings, no FPT (or W-hardness) classification for the binary Hamming weight version over F_p^* appears to have been established.

status_evidence.title: FPT suspects and tough customers: Open problems of Downey and Fellows
status_evidence.snippet: Bounded Hamming Weight Discrete Logarithm ... Open. The problem is in XP since x has at most kn bits.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open parameterized-complexity problem, known to be in XP.

status_evidence.title: On the Bounded Sum-of-Digits Discrete Logarithm Problem in Finite Fields
status_evidence.snippet: the bounded sum-of-digits discrete logarithm can be computed in random time O(f(w) log^4 q) ... hence the problem is fixed parameter tractable.
status_evidence.claim: A related sum-of-digits variant is known to be FPT, but the binary Hamming weight case over F_p^* is not resolved by this.

status_evidence.title: Computing Low-Weight Discrete Logarithms
status_evidence.snippet: improvements over meet-in-the-middle algorithms for low Hamming weight discrete logarithms
status_evidence.claim: Best known algorithms remain exponential-type rather than FPT in k.
